title: Anthropic Is Now Worth $965 Billion. Its Indian-Origin CFO Says the Demand Is 'Historic.'
excerpt: The Claude maker has overtaken OpenAI to become the world's most valuable AI startup. Krishna Rao is steering its finances as it approaches a trillion-dollar valuation.
body:
Anthropic, the San Francisco-based artificial intelligence company behind the Claude AI platform, has raised $65 billion in a Series H funding round that values the company at $965 billion — overtaking rival OpenAI to become the world’s most valuable AI startup.

The round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks, and Sequoia Capital, with co-leads including Coatue and ICONIQ. It also includes $15 billion in previously committed investments from hyperscalers, including $5 billion from Amazon. The valuation is more than double the $380 billion Anthropic secured in its February Series G round.

## Revenue Has Exploded

The company said its run-rate revenue crossed $47 billion earlier in May, up from roughly $10 billion in full-year revenue in 2025. That growth has been driven largely by enterprise adoption of Claude, which is now deployed across Amazon Web Services, Google Cloud, and Microsoft Azure.

Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao, who has emerged as a key figure in the company’s financial strategy, said the funding will help Anthropic “serve the historic demand we are experiencing, stay at the research frontier, and bring Claude to more of the places where work happens.”

Rao’s prominence at Anthropic is part of a broader pattern of Indian-origin executives shaping the AI industry at its highest levels. From Sundar Pichai at Alphabet to Satya Nadella at Microsoft to Arvind Krishna at IBM, Indian-origin leaders now hold the reins at companies collectively worth trillions of dollars. Rao’s role as CFO of what is now the most valuable AI startup in history adds another name to that list.

## The Coding Tool That Changed Everything

Much of Anthropic’s explosive growth traces back to Claude Code, a developer-focused coding assistant that has become indispensable for software teams. The company also launched Cowork, sometimes called “Claude Code for knowledge workers,” which targets non-technical enterprise users. Together, the two products have driven roughly 80 percent of the company’s revenue through enterprise channels.

Anthropic has also signed major compute infrastructure deals. The company has agreements with Amazon for up to 5 gigawatts of new capacity, with Google and Broadcom for 5 gigawatts of next-generation TPU capacity, and with SpaceX for access to GPU clusters in Colossus 1 and Colossus 2.

## Safety Concerns Loom

The funding comes alongside growing scrutiny of Anthropic’s most powerful model, Claude Mythos, which the company itself has described as having advanced cybersecurity capabilities that could be dangerous if widely released. Under a government-coordinated initiative called Project Glasswing, Amazon, Microsoft, and Apple are permitted to use Mythos for cybersecurity purposes, but broader release remains restricted.

Anthropic also released Claude Opus 4.8 this week, which the company says is more honest about uncertainty and less likely to make unsupported claims — a direct response to criticism that AI models too often project false confidence.

## IPO on the Horizon

Both Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly preparing for public offerings, possibly as early as this year. SpaceX, which houses Elon Musk’s AI outfit, recently filed IPO paperwork targeting a $1.5 trillion valuation. The convergence of these listings could reshape the tech landscape and test whether investors are willing to pay startup-era premiums for companies that are still spending far more than they earn.

For Anthropic, the near-trillion-dollar valuation is a statement. A company founded in 2021 by former OpenAI researchers Dario and Daniela Amodei has, in just five years, built a platform that enterprises consider mission-critical. Whether it can sustain that trajectory through a public offering — and through the intense safety scrutiny its own models invite — will define the next chapter of the AI race.

*Sources: Reuters, Inc., PYMNTS, The Hindu BusinessLine*
